turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, sorry, the auto got stuck near the market, that is why we are late. Kabir has got fever and cough, he is just not himself.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Since when?
[SEG0003] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Um, two days. I was going to say three, but no, it started night before last, so two days only.
[SEG0004] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No, not two. He has been warm from Monday. Today is Friday, that is four days. I was the one sitting with him.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): How high?
[SEG0006] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): 101 Fahrenheit. I put the thermometer in the armpit, it was 101, it did not cross that.
[SEG0007] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Last night it touched 103. I saw the digital reading myself. You had gone to heat the milk.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Cough?
[SEG0009] person_4 (PATIENT): No cough.
[SEG0010] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He does, doctor, he is only saying that. Dry cough, worse at night, he wakes once or twice, daytime it is mild unless he runs about.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fast breathing?
[SEG0012] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. I watched, no sucking in of the chest, breathing is comfortable.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Vomiting?
[SEG0014] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No vomiting at all.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Loose motions?
[SEG0016] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No, motions are normal. What is there is he is not eating. His upma he left, and he loves upma.

[SEG0017] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Appetite is down since this started, yes. And the throat, he has been pointing here since morning. Yesterday he refused dosa, he usually eats two, then he only wanted juice, and I was telling his father that the maid didn't come so the kitchen was—
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Where does it hurt?
[SEG0019] person_4 (PATIENT): Throat. I want the red juice, Dadi's one, not milk.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Runny nose?
[SEG0021] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yes, watery, since yesterday, mild only. He wipes it on the sleeve, I have told him so many times.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any rash on the body?
[SEG0023] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No rash.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Wheeze, any noisy breathing?
[SEG0025] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Not now. Last winter he wheezed once, they nebulised him in the clinic, one time, then it settled. Nothing like that this time.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): What syrup did you give?

[SEG0027] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Crocin, the paracetamol syrup, 250 mg in 5 ml. One teaspoon, meaning 5 ml, every six hours. Three doses yesterday and one this morning. Nothing else, I am very particular.

[SEG0028] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That bottle was Ibugesic. Ibuprofen. I gave one spoon last night when you were asleep. The big steel kitchen spoon, maybe 10 ml, I am not sure exactly. Not the small medicine spoon.
[SEG0029] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Dadi, I said not to use that spoon. Now I myself don't know which bottle it was. The labels are both yellow, that is the problem, I should have marked them.
[SEG0030] person_4 (PATIENT): Spoon yuck.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any other medicine at home?
[SEG0032] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No antibiotics, no regular medicines. He is not asthmatic, that winter thing was once only.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Is he passing urine normally?
[SEG0034] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yes, normal amount, no burning.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sleeping?

[SEG0036] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Broken sleep from the cough. Daytime he is tired, just sits, he didn't go to play cricket, and he never misses cricket, even when it is hot he is the first one down with the bat—
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay. Mouth open.
[SEG0038] person_4 (PATIENT): Aa.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): Throat is red. Ears are clear. Chest is clear, no crackles and no wheeze.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Temperature is 38.2, pulse 120, oxygen 98 percent, respiratory rate 24.
[SEG0041] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Is 38.2 serious? I only know Fahrenheit, my sister keeps sending me those conversion charts on WhatsApp, very confusing.
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): Moderate fever. This looks like a viral upper respiratory infection.
[SEG0043] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The neighbour boy had pneumonia and got admitted, so we rushed. It is not that, no?
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): Chest is clear, so I am not calling it pneumonia. I cannot fully exclude an early bacterial throat infection.
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): No blood test now. If the fever is still there after three days, we might do a blood count.
[SEG0046] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And which syrup to continue? I don't want to give the wrong one again.

[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): Only paracetamol. 5 ml of the 250 mg per 5 ml syrup, by mouth, every six hours when he is febrile. Do not give ibuprofen on top. Fluids, light food, and watch his breathing.
[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come back if he is not better in three days, earlier if the breathing turns fast.

[SEG0049] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I will keep that big spoon away from the medicines. Doctor, one more thing, he had idli this morning, two bites only, then he pushed the plate. We live together, joint family, so timings get mixed up, that is how the syrups also got mixed.
[SEG0050] person_4 (PATIENT): Home now?
